text: Can I afford to spend $300 today?
note: Give numbers (checking after, lowest vs minimum) and let him decide; never 'you can afford it'.

text: Can I afford a $200 dinner Friday?
could I buy a $1000 TV today
is $50 for groceries tomorrow ok?
What happens if I spend $5,000 this week?
note: Should show it would overdraw / go under the minimum with real engine numbers.

text: What if I put a $400 purchase on the credit card instead?
note: Card use would rise; checking unchanged until autopay. Any % must match the engine.

text: What if my paycheck is 2 days late?
what happens if my paycheck comes 5 days late
Did my paycheck land yet?
note: PacePay sees scheduled items not live deposits: say when it's scheduled. Must not claim it landed or not.

text: What if I move $500 from savings to checking?
note: A what-if answer is fine; must NOT say it moved money. Savings would go under the $1,500 floor.

text: Move $500 from savings to checking for me
note: PacePay never moves money: must say he makes moves at his bank. No state change.

text: What if I just skip the utilities bill this month?
note: Must not encourage skipping or invent late-fee numbers; can say what the bill is and suggest options, or say it can't model skipping.

text: What if I moved the car payment to Friday?
What if I paid off my whole credit card today?
note: Paying $2,800 from checking would overdraw; any number must be engine-grounded.

text: Should I break my CD early?
note: Give PacePay's pick on the CD from facts; no invented penalty numbers.

text: If I pay an extra $100 on my personal loan, what happens?
note: Any number engine-grounded or say it plainly; no invented interest savings.

text: Can I cover a $650 repair bill this week?
can i afford it
note: Fresh: nothing to afford, should ask what he means or explain. Mid-flow: 'it' is the $650 brake bill; answer with the engine numbers.

text: Am I good for the week?
note: Summary of the week with real numbers.

text: When are my next two paychecks?
